chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Atiyyah, Abu Nab, the seller of Sabir, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while he was saying: 'Whoever visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), Allah will record for him a Hajj and an Umrah, or an Umrah and a Hajj.'
I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, so what should I say when I visit him?'

He said: 'You say: Peace be upon you, O Abu Abdillah. Peace be upon you, O son of the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you on the day you were born, and on the day you die, and on the day you are raised alive. I bear witness that you are alive and a martyr, provided with sustenance by your Lord.'

And I affirm allegiance to your wali, and I declare disavowal of your enemy, and I bear witness that those who fought you and violated your sanctity are cursed upon the tongue of the Unlettered Prophet.
And I bear witness that you established the Salat, gave the Zakat, commanded what is right, forbade what is wrong, and strove in the path of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction.
I ask Allah, your wali and our wali, to make our gift from your visitation the Salat upon our Prophet and forgiveness for our sins.
Intercede for me, O son of the Messenger of Allah, with your Lord.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the theological significance of Ziyarat al-Husayn as a means of attaining the reward of Hajj and Umrah, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the living spiritual presence of the Imams. The prescribed supplication integrates key Shia doctrines, including the concept of *Hayat al-Barzakh* (life in the grave) and *Tawalli wa Tabarri* (affiliation with friends and enmity with foes), while invoking the Prophet’s intercession. This narrative underscores the grave as a locus of divine mercy and a point of connection between the earthly community and the celestial hierarchy.
